claim: Joanna C. Schwartz, How Qualified Immunity Fails, 127 Yale L.J. 2 (2017), found only about 0.6% of cases were dismissed at the motion-to-dismiss stage on qualified-immunity grounds.
evidence: just seven (0.6%) were dismissed at the motion to dismiss stage
excerpt: The Supreme Court’s decisions suggest another theory that could partially explain why qualified immunity disposes of few cases: because courts improperly deny defendants’ qualified immunity motions.
